Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Nature & food

severe adjective

of weather, pain or hardship: harsh, hard to bear

also harsh (of weather), a severe winter, severe cold, severe pain, bitter (of cold), sharp (of pain)

classical

Hor. C. 1.4.1: solvitur ācris hiems
Plaut. Men. 5.2.119: morbum ācrem ac dūrum (Lewis & Short)

ācer, ācris, ācre

adjective, third declension, three endings · Declension on Wiktionary

sharp, severe (of winter, pain, hunger)

Sharp and piercing: a sharp winter (Ennius, Horace), sharp pain, hunger, thirst (Lewis & Short). Its main senses are sharp, keen, eager: of a person it means keen or fierce, not strict (see severe, of a person). For a severe illness or wound the usual word is gravis (see serious).

Other words

  • dūrus, dūra, dūrum — hard to bear, harsh

    adjective · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 7.8.2: dūrissimō tempore annī; Verg. A. 5.5: dūrī … dolōrēs (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Hard to bear: the hardest time of the year, hard pains, hard poverty (Lewis & Short).

  • asper, aspera, asperum — rough, harsh (of winter, sea, climate)

    adjective · also used · classical · Ov. M. 11.490: hiems (Lewis & Short); Tac. G. 2: aspera caelō, harsh in climate (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Rough to the touch, and so rough and harsh: a rough sea, a harsh winter, a harsh country.

Examples

  • Solvitur ācris hiems grātā vice vēris et Favōnī

    harsh winter is loosening its grip as spring and the west wind come round in welcome turnHor. C. 1.4.1

  • mōns Cevenna … dūrissimō tempore annī altissimā nive iter impediēbat

    at the hardest time of the year the Cévennes blocked the way with very deep snowCaes. B.G. 7.8.2

See also severe, serious, winter, cold.
